newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks advance in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks advance in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks marched ahead in active trade, boosted by positive Wall Street sentiment and a favourable assessment of the Cheung Kong group's reorganisation, brokers said.
"Sentiment in the U.S. is very bullish, said Jason Tang in institutional sales at South China Securities. "There is no sign of caution despite the long bond yield is going to 6.8 percent."
The Hang Seng Index added 50 points in early trade to 13,470 on heavy turnover of HK$1.84 billion, augmented by active trade in the Cheung Kong group.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 33.48 points to a new record close of 6,600.66, together with the tech-studded Nasdaq Composite Index, which ended 11.33 points higher at a new record of 1,327.73. But the bond market was more cautious with the benchmark U.S. 30-year long bond easing down 7/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
"There is a divergence in the U.S. equity and bond markets," said Steven Chu, technical analyst at Sassoon Securities.
"The generally positive sentiment on Wall St will boost the Hong Kong market at the open, but if the bond yield is high it will bring the market down later in the day," added Chu.
The January Hang Seng Index futures contract put on 80 points to trade at 13,475.
The property sector led the market followed at a distance by finance.
Cheung Kong was the most actively traded issue on heavy turnover of HK$262 million in the first half hour of trade. The share added HK$1.75 to HK$74.50.

Brokers said the share had lagged the trend of other developers, such as Henderson Land and Sun Hung Kai Properties, due chiefly to its lack of transparency. They added that Monday's announced reorganisation was expected to yield further developments and announcements.

Hutchison Whampoa was also actively traded with trade reaching HK$152 million. The share gained HK$1.00 to HK$68.00. Cheung Kong Infrastructure added HK$0.30 to HK$21.55, while Hongkong Electric shed HK$0.50 to HK$27.10.
Brokers said Hutchison's general offer price of HK$26.50 for Hongkong Electric served to cap near-term upside for the share.
Sun Hung Kai Properties advanced HK$1.00 to HK$95.25 , while Great Eagle lost HK$0.70 to HK33.40.
HSBC Holdings jumped HK$1.00 to HK$168.50, its all-time high, then eased to trade HK$0.50 higher at HK$167.50.
